summary: Chapters 0-8 of book.md (lines 141-2911, roughly 22,800 words of prose plus about 240 display equations) take a reader from a cart on a track to the Riemann tensor of a sphere. The order is: measurement-led calculus and mechanics (Ch 0), free fall/scale/accelerometer/two-ball tides and clock comparison with no equations of GR (Ch 1), vectors/covectors/Jacobians/tensors through a doubled basis vector (Ch 2), special relativity derived from light signals with interval, proper time, twin, four-momentum and observer energy E=-p.U (Ch 3), charts/atlas/tangent vectors/metric/inverse metric/volume element (Ch 4), proper acceleration, equivalence principle, Rindler clocks, and the geodesic equation derived from the worldline action with null/affine subtleties and the Newtonian limit (Ch 5), covariant derivative from a fixed arrow in a rotating basis plus divergence, wave operator and Lie bracket (Ch 6), parallel transport, Levi-Civita uniqueness, Christoffel transformation law and five flat polar-plane checks (Ch 7), and curvature as commutator/holonomy with polar flatness, the 20-component count and the sphere (Ch 8). The science is careful and conventions are explicit and consistent: signature (-,+,+,+), x^0=ct, and a Riemann sign that gives R=2/a^2 on a sphere. I re-derived about 30 worked numbers and component results (cart 1.23 m, map dot product 14, covector pairing 11, Lorentz 4 s and -16 ls^2, simultaneity -0.75 s, twin 8 yr, oblique metric inverse and 13, spherical g=-r^4 sin^2 theta, Rindler alpha(z)=a/(1+az/c^2), all five polar-plane experiments, R^r_theta r theta=0, sphere R^theta_phi theta phi=sin^2 theta, stereographic transition check, flow-order gap h^2) and found no errors. The teaching method is consistent and strong. It separates object from components from measurement, returns again and again to flat-space counterexamples (the polar plane, Rindler, the cone), and pairs every derivation with a numerical check. The main weaknesses are pedagogical, not scientific. Chapter 0 is a thin refresher, not a physics on-ramp. Chapters 2-8 have almost no in-text exercises: assessment lives in guides.json checks and 15 external bridge lessons. A few key steps are asserted rather than shown (the holonomy formula in 8.3, the cancellation of first-derivative terms in 8.1, locally inertial coordinates in 4.8). Seven 'Further calculation/example' disclosures reuse the history-note class and data-no-narration, so optional-looking blocks (the sphere area-rotation derivation, the cut cone, rapidity) are both collapsed and skipped by narration. Several passages also narrate demo outcomes ('The animation below' in 1.10, 'the plane and rolled sheet returned the arrow unchanged' at the Ch 8 opening), so the prose cannot be ported without its demos or a rewrite of those sentences. The text is also coupled to the old build through six data-*-insert placeholders and five build-specific links (course-map.html, #polar-coordinates, chapter-6.html#flow-order, chapter-6.html#6-6-..., chapter-7.html#parallel-transport-lab). The §8.3 small-loop sign was checked by hand in review: it agrees with the optional area derivation and with the octant example. Novice readiness was repaired in a documented audit but never tested with learners. Overall verdict: the prose is the most valuable reusable asset in this range. Adapt it into grbook.ai lessons section by section, keeping derivations and worked checks nearly verbatim while adding practice, stable concept IDs and live demos.
lessons_learned: First-use discipline failed silently before it was enforced. docs/novice-sequencing-audit-2026-09-09.md records premature 'metric', 'connection coefficients', 'Ricci/Weyl' and 'proper time' in Chapters 0-3 and a Chapter 0 opener that used polar metrics. The fix was a rewrite plus a narrow keyword guard (scripts/check-learning-sequence.mjs line 35). grbook.ai needs a concept registry in which each section declares introduced and required concepts and a build check rejects use before introduction. A keyword blacklist is not enough.

Placement matters as much as prose. The old publisher put every one of the 36 worked lessons directly after its section heading, which was before the exposition they used. An editorial classification then found that 26 of them belong after their section's exposition and 10 are genuine preparation (docs/novice-sequencing-audit-2026-09-09.md line 11). The audit explicitly says this is a placement count, not a count of incomprehensible lessons. Separately, 8 labs were inserted above chapter prose (reading-quality-pass 'Interface and sequencing'). Of the 37 placements now listed in content/lesson-sequence.mjs, 15 belong to Ch 0-8 and 14 of those are 'section-end'; the exception is flows-that-do-not-commute at the start of 7.2. Anchor every demo or practice unit to a section and a side (before/after), each with a written reason, as lesson-sequence.mjs does, and check it against declared 'provides'/'requires' concepts.

A single recurring flat-space counterexample thread is the pedagogical backbone of Ch 4-8 and should become an explicit spine in the new course: polar plane in 4.2 (grid lab), metric 4.5, frame 4.8, rotating basis 6.1, five checks 7.5, zero curvature 8.4. Alongside it run Rindler (5.3) and the cut cone (8.3). Each shows nonzero Christoffels, coordinate acceleration or clock-rate differences with zero curvature.

Optional-looking disclosures carry load-bearing content, and the markup hides it twice. In Ch 0-8 there are 8 <details class="history-note" data-no-narration> blocks. Only the one in 1.9 is history. The other seven are 'Further calculation/example' blocks: 2.6 oriented area, 3.3 rapidity, 4.1 topology, 5.7 einbein, 6.6 polar-frame bracket, 8.3 sphere area-rotation, and 8.3 cut cone. They are collapsed by default and skipped by narration, so a listener to the narrated book never hears the only quantitative holonomy derivation. The sinh/cosh case is softer than it first looks. §5.3 says the functions were 'introduced in §3.3', a pointer into the optional block, but it then restates both definitions and their derivatives inline. The old course also supplied them through the core lesson hyperbolas-and-rapidity (content/foundation-lessons.mjs, provides 'hyperbolic-functions'). grbook.ai needs a real depth model (core / worked detail / further) with a narration policy per depth and a rule that core text may not point into further-depth material.

The manuscript has almost no active practice. Only Chapters 0 and 1 contain in-text checkpoints: five in 0.9 and prediction reveals in 1.1 and 1.8. Chapters 2-8 contain none, and 2.6 only advises the reader to 'practice expanding'. Assessment lives in the nine open reveal-answer checks in content/guides.json plus 15 external lessons attached to Ch 0-8. The review's F03 finding (all 13 multiple-choice checks put the correct answer at index 0) applies to those lesson files (geometry-lessons.mjs, bridge-lessons.mjs), not to guides.json. grbook.ai should generate predict / complete-a-step / calculate / diagnose items from worked examples that already exist, for example the five 7.5 experiments, the 8.6 sphere and the 4.6 oblique metric. The AI tutor should grade the method as well as the number, and any multiple-choice ordering should be shuffled reproducibly.

Worked numbers can be checked cheaply, and the legacy repo only partly did so (check-learning-sequence.mjs asserts the cart 1.23 m and the Lorentz 4 s / -16 results). Every numeric and component claim in Ch 0-8 is short enough to encode as a unit test. Do this when porting so the AI tutor and narration can cite verified values.

Build coupling in the source must be stripped, and anchor stability must be kept rather than thrown away. Ch 0-8 of book.md contain 1 data-mechanics-insert (0.5) and 5 data-foundation-insert placeholders: polar 4.2, vector-field 6.1, flow-order 6.6, transport 7.1, transport-routes at the Ch 8 opening. They also contain five build-specific links: course-map.html, #polar-coordinates, chapter-6.html#flow-order, chapter-6.html#6-6-..., and chapter-7.html#parallel-transport-lab. content/section-ids.json is not stale by accident. It is a deliberate map from section number to frozen anchor that keeps saved links and prerequisite destinations working after heading edits (reading-quality-pass 'Section IDs are preserved'; check-site.mjs validates it; check-learning-sequence.mjs even looks up '3-3-the-interval-the-quantity-that-refuses-to-change'). grbook.ai should keep the idea with opaque stable section and concept IDs, and never derive anchors from heading text.

Conventions stated once and used consistently prevent sign drift. The reading-guide conventions block (book.md 35-100) fixes signature, x^0=ct, the Riemann convention and the Einstein-Hilbert normalization, and §8.6 ties the sign to R=2/a^2. Carry this block and its operational sphere check into the knowledge vault as the canonical convention sheet.

Honest status labels are a strength worth keeping as house style: 'this is a preview, not a derivation' (5.8), 'counting components is not counting propagating modes' (4.4, 8.5), 'the equivalence principle does not uniquely imply Einstein's equation' (5.2), 'analogies are scaffolding' (book.md 29). The AI tutor's system prompt should require the same qualification habits.

Expert review and automated checks overstated novice readiness until a reader complaint exposed it (comprehensive-course-review follow-up note). Chapters 2 and 4-8 have had only targeted, not complete, first-use audits (novice audit 'Remaining teaching review'). Budget a learner-observation pass before calling the ported Ch 0-8 novice-ready.

The prose narrates demo outcomes, so text and demo must be ported together. §1.10 opens 'The animation below draws lines between imagined small laboratories' and spends four paragraphs on how to read that river-model grid. §4.5 begins 'Return to the angular-step view in the polar-coordinate experiment'. §6.6 says 'First watch the two routes'. The Ch 8 opening asserts what the Ch 7 transport lab showed. When a grbook.ai demo changes what it shows, these sentences must be rewritten; a concept-ID link alone will not fix them. Track demo-dependent sentences explicitly in the port.

Sign conventions are checkable by hand, and this one checks out. Using the book's convention, R^phi_theta theta phi = -1 on the unit-radius sphere chart. The loop order +theta, +phi, -theta, -phi then gives a unit-arrow rotation Delta psi = +sin theta Delta theta Delta phi, the same as the optional tiling derivation. The octant route in §8.3 (equator to pole, down a meridian 90 degrees east, back along the equator) traverses the opposite orientation, so Delta psi = -pi/2. That turns a north-pointing arrow (psi = pi, since north = -e_theta) into an east-pointing one (psi = pi/2), as the text says. Encode this as a regression test: an orientation slip here would silently flip geodesic deviation later.

assets.title: Chapter 0. Measurements and motion
assets.teaches: Entry refresher for a reader with basic calculus and linear algebra. Velocity as a local prediction with a numeric acceleration correction (1.2 m vs exact 1.23 m). Partial derivatives and the two-input chain rule. Integral as summed local measurements (tank volume, mass from density). Why a second-order ODE needs two initial data. Force, work, kinetic and potential energy, a spring energy exchange, and the Newtonian potential with a = -grad Phi. Pressure. A calibrated map turned into a bilinear form v^T M w (a proto-metric). Box-face flux leading to divergence and mass conservation. First-order estimates with a small parameter. Five checks with answers.
assets.pedagogy: Measurement-led sequence: position/time, velocity/acceleration, units, partials, integrals, ODE data, force/energy, matrix measurement, flux, approximation (novice audit 'What now comes first'). Every concept gets a concrete number before the general formula. Deliberately free of relativity vocabulary (enforced by a keyword check). The spring subsection hands off to an embedded mechanics energy lab (data-mechanics-insert=energy). Three bridge lessons attach at 0.1, 0.4 and 0.5. Section 0.9 offers five reveal-answer checks and an explicit skip route for experienced readers.
assets.physics_model: Newtonian mechanics, SI units, constant mass. Spring example: 1 kg, k=1 N/m, 1 m stretch, 0.5 J, peak speed 1 m/s. Near-Earth fall g=9.8 m/s^2, no drag. Outside a sphere Phi=-G_N M/r. Numeric claims re-derived during this inventory. The cart correction is also asserted in scripts/check-learning-sequence.mjs.
